cards.text: The tabernacle is finally up, and the glory of the LORD has filled it (Exodus 40:34). Now the LORD calls to Moses, Israel's leader, and speaks to him from the Tent of Meeting. He has a message for the Israelites about bringing Him offerings.

cards.question: When one of the Israelites brings an animal as an offering to the LORD, where can it come from?

cards.text: First up, the burnt offering. If it comes from the herd, it can't just be the one with the limp that nobody wants, because God says exactly what to bring.

cards.question: What does a man have to bring from his herd for a burnt offering?
Where does the man bring his burnt offering so it can be accepted before the LORD?

answers.text: The entrance to the Tent of Meeting
The bank of the Jordan River

cards.text: Now here's the moment. He can't just drop it off like a cookie box on a porch and run. He walks up and lays his hand on the animal's head.

cards.question: The man lays his hand on the head of his burnt offering. Why?

answers.text: So it can make atonement for him
So the priest knows it is his
So it stays calm at the altar

cards.text: Then he slaughters the young bull before the LORD. Now the blood has to go on the altar, and this part isn't his job.

cards.question: Who splatters the bull's blood on all sides of the altar?

cards.text: He skins it and cuts it into pieces. The priests build the fire, arrange the wood and lay every piece on top, head and fat included, and friend, that's more careful arranging than I've ever done with a tray of sprinkles.

cards.question: Before the entrails and legs of the burnt offering go on the altar, they get washed with water.
Once everything is on the altar, how much of the burnt offering does the priest burn?

cards.text: The LORD calls it "a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD." Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer smelling old takeout menus and dust, so I RESPECT a pleasing aroma.

cards.question: No animal from the herd? A burnt offering from the flock can be ___ or ___.
The animal from the flock is slaughtered before the LORD. Which side of the altar does that happen on?

cards.text: From there it goes just like the bull: cut into pieces, washed, all of it burned, and that line again about a "pleasing aroma." Then the LORD gives one more option for a burnt offering, and this one has wings.

cards.question: Which birds can someone bring as a burnt offering to the LORD?

answers.text: A turtledove or a young pigeon
A raven or a young eagle
A sparrow or a young quail

cards.text: The priest brings the bird to the altar, twists off its head and drains the blood on the side of the altar. He throws the crop to the east side, in the place for ashes.

cards.question: The priest divides the bird completely in two before he burns it on the altar.

cards.text: Now the LORD moves from animals to grain, and friend, I'm a cookie stamper. This is my DEPARTMENT, and it starts with fine flour.

cards.question: For a grain offering, the person bringing it pours ___ on the fine flour and puts ___ on it.

cards.text: He brings it to the priests. The priest takes a handful of the flour and oil, with all the frankincense, and burns it on the altar as a memorial portion.

cards.question: The priest burned a handful of the grain offering as a memorial portion. What happens to the rest?

answers.text: It belongs to Aaron and his sons
It goes back to the man who brought it
It gets burned the next morning

cards.text: Then the LORD covers the cooking options: baked in an oven, made on a griddle or cooked in a pan. He said OVEN, friend, and I have been waiting this WHOLE lesson for that word.

cards.question: Oven, griddle or pan, what goes into every one of these grain offerings?
The grain offering made on a griddle gets crumbled, with oil poured on it.

cards.text: Any way it's made, it goes to the priest, who burns the memorial portion, and the rest belongs to Aaron and his sons. Then the LORD draws a line about what never goes up in smoke.

cards.question: No ___ or ___ may be burned as a food offering to the LORD.
Leaven and honey can still be brought to the LORD as an offering of firstfruits, as long as they don't go up on the altar.

cards.text: Next, the LORD names one thing every grain offering has to be seasoned with. Leaving it out is NOT an option.

cards.question: What must every grain offering be seasoned with?

cards.text: He calls it "the salt of the covenant of your God," and it goes in every offering. Last one: a grain offering of firstfruits.

cards.question: For a grain offering of firstfruits, what does the LORD say to bring?

answers.text: Crushed new grain roasted on fire
Whole barley soaked in cold water

cards.question: The firstfruits grain offering gets oil and frankincense too, and the priest burns its memorial portion.

cards.text: Now a new one: the peace offering. It can come from the herd too, and the LORD says what kind of animal works.

cards.question: For a peace offering from the herd, what kind of animal can it be?

answers.text: A male or female without blemish

cards.question: Just like with the burnt offering, the man lays his hand on the head of his peace offering.

cards.text: He slaughters it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and the priests splatter the blood on all sides of the altar.

cards.question: From the peace offering, what does the man bring as a food offering to the LORD?

answers.text: The fat and kidneys and liver lobe
The head and legs and hide
The whole animal and its skin

cards.text: Aaron's sons burn it on the altar, right on top of the burnt offering on the burning wood. And you know the line by now: "a pleasing aroma to the LORD."
From the flock it's the same: male or female without blemish, hand on the head, blood on the altar. But if it's a lamb, there's one extra piece of fat on the list.

cards.question: What extra piece of fat comes off a lamb brought as a peace offering?

cards.text: A goat works the same way: hand on its head, blood on the altar, and the same fat and kidneys and liver lobe come off for the LORD. Every step spelled out, and friend, I once burned a whole batch with the timer RINGING right in my face.

cards.question: After the priest burns the goat's portion on the altar, the LORD says: All the ___ is the LORD's.

cards.text: Then the LORD closes with one more rule for the Israelites, and it's a big one.

cards.question: The LORD's rule for the Israelites: You must not eat any ___ or any ___.
The LORD says the rule about not eating fat or blood only lasts while Israel is camped around the tabernacle.

cards.text: A permanent statute, for the generations to come, wherever they live. And friend, the LORD isn't done teaching about offerings yet, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: This whole passage is rules for offerings, and "rules for offerings and feasts" is listed as a long stretch, which gets one summary story card and no choice cards. It is also all one speech from the LORD to Moses, and "speeches, teaching and key laws" are listed as not a long stretch. The walkthrough treats it as heart content: 3 stops and 31 choice cards. The docs don't say what to do when the entire passage is itself a long stretch, or a speech made of long-stretch material.
findings.question: When a whole passage is offering rules spoken as one speech from the LORD, should it be taught with full story and choice cards like a speech or key law, or summed up like a long stretch? If summed up, how should a passage that is only a stretch be built?

findings.problem: Three two-blank fill-in-the-blank cards have blanks that can swap places without changing the meaning: stop 1 card 14 (sheep ___ or goats ___), stop 2 card 9 (leaven ___ or honey ___) and stop 3 card 12 (fat ___ or blood ___). Each right answer is locked to one blank. A baker who puts "goats" in blank 1 and "sheep" in blank 2 gives an equally true answer but would be marked as missing it.
findings.question: Are two-blank cards allowed when the two right answers are an unordered pair ("X or Y")? If so, should either order count as right, or should these cards be reworded so each blank has only one possible word?

findings.problem: Aaron is first named here, in the right answer "Aaron's sons the priests," and never introduced. No story card says who Aaron is, for example Moses's brother, Israel's high priest (Exodus 28:1). He appears again in stop 2 cards 4 and 8 and stop 3 card 6, still without an introduction.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the fact's action. The fact is the goat offering's steps being spelled out the same way. The comparison is Papa Dorin burning a batch while the timer rang. Ignoring a ringing timer isn't the same action as having every step spelled out, so the link takes explaining. In a passage about burning offerings on an altar, "burned a whole batch" also blurs into the Bible setting.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Stop 3 has almost no humor. Its only joke is the one on card 9, which misfires. The other story cards (1, 4, 6, 7, 11, 14) are plain retelling or mild lines like "keep that apron on." Stop 3 reads like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
